observedBehavior: The source index records an end line and parser provenance for FastAPI handlers and supported TypeScript/JavaScript handlers and calls.
A selected diff returns a baseline file hash and changed hunk coordinates, without source or patch text.

An indexed span is labeled overlapping only when its source file hash matches the selected diff old-side blob and a hunk intersects its old-side range. Tests distinguish commit, staged-index and unstaged-index baselines.
When the index hash is stale, the assessment falls back to file association; same-file targets remain visible.
The real Orders defect was located in the indexed handler; Billing's missing check, failed receipts, stale proof and incomplete repaired ledger remained visible.
limitations: FastAPI end lines use indentation heuristics; TypeScript/JavaScript spans use AST ranges. Neither establishes a semantic response-contract delta.
Only eligible, bounded tracked text files have baseline hashes and hunk ranges. Unsupported paths remain file-level potential impacts.
Consumer links in the runtime fixture are seeded from inspected source; independent discovery, owner coverage and test relevance are incomplete.
Temporary fixture repositories and package manifests are deleted; the redacted report alone cannot reproduce those commits.
Team parity, permission-revocation, browser/keyboard and full D1/D2 release gates remain open.
